This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. People on the Gulf Coast are being
urged to take shelter as Hurricane Isaias barrels ahead. It's the first hurricane of
an unusually quiet Atlantic season, NPR's Sergio Martinez-Beltranz in Pensacola, Florida.
Conditions in the Florida panhandle have quickly deteriorated. The wind has picked up. The rain
is becoming more intense in this area. State officials have said they're hoping that it
will weaken by the time it hits the shore. Governor Dicente said the state has prepared
to respond to it as a major hurricane. Sergio Martinez-Beltranz, NPR News, Pensacola, Florida.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky says the White House's decision to lift sanctions
on Russian diesel will only prolong the war. NPR's Joanna Kakesis reports that President
Trump announced the deal after speaking with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump's
decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel is the White House's latest attempt to lower
fuel prices, which have risen sharply since the U.S. war on Iran. In a voice message to
reporters, Zelensky slams Trump's decision as weak and says Russia will make billions.
That means more money for this war, more money to inflict suffering on us, he said. It only
feeds Putin and gives him the ability to keep fighting. Ukraine's negotiating team is in
Florida trying to restart peace talks. Zelensky says the team is being used as "a smokescreen."
Joanna Kakesis, NPR News, CAVE. Senior ICE official Marcos Charles says federal officers
shot and wounded a Dominican man in New York yesterday because they believe their lives
were in danger. ICE officers shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgaal in the neck while he was driving
with his 5-year-old son. DHS says the officers didn't see the child. Vice President J.D.
Vance expressed doubts today about the Pentagon's plan to livestream the firing squad execution
of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hassan.
I hope that people don't forget that this is a guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent
people. Now, that said, I mean, look, if it's ultimately livestreamed, I'm not going to
be watching it. Hassan killed 13 people and injured 32 others during a mass shooting at
Fort Hood Army Base in Texas. The U.S. has not conducted a public execution since the
1930s. Public executions are rare globally. Only Iran and Afghanistan carried out public
executions last year.
Families headed by someone aged 75 or older are now America's wealthiest, while the youngest
families saw their wealth decline in the past three years. That's according to the Federal
Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances. It underscores how robust stock market gains
have made wealthier American families even richer since the survey conducted every three
years was last completed in 2022.
This is NPR News.
Authorities in the United Arab Emirates say the fly Dubai co-pilot attacked the captain
of a flight to Tel Aviv last month intending to crash the plane into Israel's main airport
terminal. The UAE's top prosecutor says the Omani National aimed to cause maximum casualties
drawing inspiration from the September 11th attacks. The co-pilot confessed to acting
alone. President Trump has announced a $100 million program to support individuals who
pursue PhDs in STEM research. NPR's Alyssa Nadwirny reports this new push comes as the
administration has created a lot of uncertainty around scientific research.
The White House says it is ushering in "a golden age of science research." That includes
a shift away from federal funding and toward private industry investment. But no Ross,
a scientist who co-founded GrantWitness, an organization that tracks federal grant funding,
sees it differently.
"I am always enthusiastic about more investment into science, but you could think of this
as someone planting a tree somewhere where they just burned down a forest, right?"
In the last two years, the Trump administration has canceled or paused more than $11 billion
federal research money to universities. Labs shut down, projects halted, researchers let
go — and that's fed into a feeling that U.S. scientific research is falling behind
countries like China. Alyssa Nadwirny, NPR News.
The Draconid meteor shower peaks tonight. It comes as Earth barrels through the debris
stream left by a comet. Unlike most meteor showers, the Draconids are best viewed in
the evening just a few hours after sunset.
I'm Rylan Barton. This is NPR News from Washington.
